<!-- pr-reviewer: ef50496e42d2b05238d2a2995724dd80427e1412 -->

**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** The code and the gates pass. Two documentation items block the merge. Both are small.

**What looks good:**
- One release build (`--no-run`), then one step per test target. This is what issue #1714 asked for.
- The plan never drops a binary by accident. A binary with a `mod` declaration, an `include!` or a `#[path]` always gets a step. Unreadable source gets a step.
- The test `heavy_steps_skip_only_binaries_without_ignored_tests` scans every file under `tests/` of motion and app. It pins that each binary with an `#[ignore]` has a step.
- The step note names the failed tests. It also names each test that libtest reports as running over 60 s.
- The old step ran `cargo test --release -p <crate> -- --ignored` as one step. The new targets cover the same set. The `#[test]` count does not change.

**Results, built locally in a worktree at the head:**
- `git merge-tree` with `origin/main`: clean, no conflicts. GitHub reports MERGEABLE.
- `cargo test -p xtask`: 131 passed, 0 failed. The four new `heavy_tests` pass.
- `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run`: 163 steps, 0 failed. 151 steps are heavy steps: `heavy build (release --no-run)`, then 21 `motion heavy: *` steps and 129 `app heavy: *` steps. The plan before this change had 2 heavy steps.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Process law: the body carries `Process change: yes`. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. The body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #1714`. The commit subjects are conventional. No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` in the new code outside test modules. The changed files stay under 400 lines.

**Requested before merge:**
1. `docs/decisions/1714-heavy-lane-steps.md:1` uses the heading `# 1714 heavy lane steps`. `docs/decisions/README.md` gives the format: a `## #N - <title>` heading. Every other decision file uses it, for example `## #1702 - ...`. `cargo xtask decisions` appends the file text unchanged under the `## vX.Y.Z` heading of `RECOMMENDED.md`. An `#` heading there breaks the document structure. Fix: change the line to `## #1714 - Plan one release heavy step for each test binary`.
2. `docs/decisions/1714-heavy-lane-steps.md:6` defers the kernel heavy lane: "Left for a follow-up." Issue #1714 names the kernel lane too. No follow-up issue exists. Fix: file one (`source:agent`, `area:build`, one `P*`, one `effort:*`), then name it in the decision file and in the PR body. AGENTS.md keeps owed work in the issues, not in prose.

**Questions / notes (not blocking):**
- Issue #1714 asks for a "stated limit" for a slow test. The build uses the fixed 60 s report of libtest on stable. A real limit needs nightly `--report-time`. The PR body discloses this. That is a fair reading of the ask.
- The release paragraph of AGENTS.md says one step for "each test target that can hold an ignored test". The `lib`, `bins` and `doc` steps are always planned; only the integration binaries are filtered. One extra sentence could say that.
- Commit `ef50496e4` restores the line endings that commit `dc42fb3ca` changed. The net diff of the PR is correct. Please keep the original endings in later pushes.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- review-cost: ef50496e42d2b05238d2a2995724dd80427e1412 -->

**Estimated agent cost:** ~$0.54 (97k tokens, estimate)

Model: session model (general-purpose review agent). Route: local build in worktree (xtask/ and AGENTS.md are pr-test refusal paths); xtask unit tests + release dry-run plan + clippy.

Blended upper estimate at list price; cache reads make the real cost lower.
